termina/crostini-pin: add new ebuilds Add two new ebuilds that pin versions of the Termina VM and the Crostini container on the rootfs. This does not have any effect outside of testing. vboot: remove tinyhostlib from Makefile vboot Makefile contains a target library called libtinyvboot_host.a, and claims it is used by autoupdate installer since it must sometimes be a 32-bit executable. (See CL:44442.) As far as I can tell, this lib is no longer used, and we can safely remove it: (1) I don't see any mention of this file in any repo's git history: $ repo list | sed -e 's@ :.*@@' | while read dir; do ( cd $dir; out=`git --no-pager log --no-renames -p -Svboot_host | grep tinyvboot_host`; [ -z "$out" ] || echo "$dir\n$out" ); done; src/platform/vboot_reference +TINYHOSTLIB = ${BUILD}/libtinyvboot_host.a (2) The library doesn't get installed in vboot_reference's ebuild. BUG=b:124141368 TEST=build vboot_reference BRANCH=none Change-Id: I0ff41f0596f911ac1d969bfabcdaab7fc2c883f7 Signed-off-by: Joel Kitching <kitching@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1535459 Commit-Ready: Joel Kitching <kitching@chromium.org> Tested-by: Joel Kitching <kitching@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Simon Glass <sjg@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

enter_chroot: bind mount /dev recursively If nodes under /dev are bind mounted themselves (e.g. how /dev is set up under Crostini containers), then bind mounting just /dev won't work to pass through the full /dev state. chromeos-bootimage: use 0xff as the padding value, more cases Chrome OS firmware images still include large padding spaces set to the value of zero, which makes programming flash chips longer. The chromeos-bootimage ebuild keeps growing, but not all relevant cbfstools invocations are passed the command line parameter requiring filling the padding area with 0xff. This patch fixes a few more instances resulting in elimination of 119K of padding zeros in atlas and fizz firmware images, other boards presumably showing similar improvements. BRANCH=none BUG=none TEST=built a new image and programmed Fizz with it, verified that it boots Chrome OS as expected Change-Id: I9ae4786e0f9a1bc1eba88224ce1884276288765b Signed-off-by: Vadim Bendebury <vbendeb@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1533284 Commit-Ready: Mathew King <mathewk@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Julius Werner <jwerner@chromium.org>

Support build artifacts for external data files. This change adds support of declaring build artifacts as external data files in the following JSON format: { "type": "artifact", "name": "license_credits.html" } If this JSON is found as *.external in data/ directory, the file at gs://chromeos-image-archive/$BUILDER_PATH/license_credits.html is downloaded to the DUT, where $BUILDER_PATH is a string found as CHROMEOS_RELEASE_BUILDER_PATH in /etc/lsb-release. Afterwards, those files can be accessible in tests with s.DataPath just like other static external data files. BUG=chromium:943383 TEST=tast run -buildlocalrunner DUT example.DataFiles TEST=fast_build.sh -T Change-Id: I70dc14c9a2a7a70bd5986c7c3677b4fac4e0e73e Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1530386 Commit-Ready: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org> Tested-by: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org>

P2P tests: Retry one, make another less strict. Sometimes when the 2nd DUT looks for the 1st DUT to update via P2P it will find another DUT in the lab with P2P enabled and use that instead of the DUT we expect. I have been failing the test in this case but I now I think it is OK since it is still actually updating via p2p and we cannot control which DUT P2P decides to use. I've added a retry to the P2P test for another issue where it cannot find any hosts sometimes. Add PackageIndexService. Postsubmit uploads package prebuilts to Google Storage. To do this, the build API must expose methods for reading and writing to the Portage package index (i.e. the Packages file generated by a build). In particular, postsubmit must be able to: - Read the list of packages built by portage. - Update the package index so that each package PATH points to its Google Storage URL. - Update binhost conf files to point to the new package index. Change-Id: Ie13455013fcdca10f4611217a8f5e1c7c64a3f67 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1531147 Commit-Ready: Evan Hernandez <evanhernandez@chromium.org> Tested-by: Evan Hernandez <evanhernandez@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Alex Klein <saklein@chromium.org>
